subject: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance

Elena — quick heads up from the platform team. We are seeing a provider-side peering degradation affecting our EU region (eu-west-2) that started ~07:40 UTC and is intermittently dropping connections to a subset of edge POPs. Impact: increased 5xx and degraded tail latency for EU-origin requests to hosted endpoints and embeddings.

Immediate recommendation (for minimal code changes):
- Prefer regional routing header: set X-Redwood-Region: us or apac where possible (clients in the EU can point to the US fallback until eu stabilizes).
- Short-term DNS override: swap primary CNAME to eu-fallback-02.redwoodapi.com (TTL 60s).
- Client-side retry policy: exponential backoff starting at 150ms, max 2 retries for non-idempotent calls.

Attached: rl-traffic-reroute_v3.pdf (operational steps your infra team can apply in the next 30–60 minutes).

CCing Monica, Marcus and Laura for capacity and post-incident follow-up. We will push a live status update to our status page and follow up with a postmortem.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com
Attachment: rl-traffic-reroute_v3.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthlytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: oncall@healthlytics.com
Date: 2028-10-04T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance

Thanks Priya — we are seeing increased 502s and a spike in user-facing latency for our EU customers. Two quick questions:
1) If we set X-Redwood-Region: us for EU-origin traffic, will there be a material change to model selection or tokenization (we rely on embed-compact-v2 for search)?
2) Can you confirm any risk to data residency? Our compliance team will want to know.

I can schedule our SRE to apply the DNS override now if you confirm the guidance.

— Elena
Elena Rossi
VP, Infrastructure — HealthLytics
elena.rossi@healthlytics.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance

Elena — good questions. Short answers:
- Model behavior: No change to model family or tokenizer. When you route to the US fallback we will serve the same model variant (embed-compact-v2) unless you have pinned a region-only variant. Token accounting and responses are identical; only latency/cost trade-offs change.
- Data residency: temporary routing to our US pool is a live-fallback only and counts toward your existing contract usage. We will NOT replicate persisted customer data across jurisdictions as part of this action; request bodies remain transient and are treated per our standard retention policy. If you require an audit note for compliance, we can provide a short attestation for this temporary failover.

Operational runbook (extracted from attachment):
1) Update client header: X-Redwood-Region: us
2) DNS swap: change primary CNAME -> eu-fallback-02.redwoodapi.com, TTL=60s
3) Circuit breaker: set 5xx threshold to 10% over 2m window to fail fast to fallback
4) Warm-up: pre-warm 4 vCPU-shard instances in us region if you expect high burst (see capacity notes below)

We expect this to reduce the 5xx surface within 10–15 minutes of change propagation. If you'd like we can make the DNS change for you (we have delegated CNAME control in your org) — otherwise confirm and your SRE can apply.

— Priya
Attachment: rl-traffic-reroute_v3.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance

Quick ops note from the serving team:
- US capacity is healthy for your current sustained QPS; warm-up recommended if you expect >2x normal traffic. Warm-up plan: 6 warm instances per shard over 12 minutes to populate KV caches.
- APAC fallback is available but currently also seeing elevated queue times; prefer US if you have low-latency tolerance.
- We will enable shorter batching windows (50ms) for your routed traffic to reduce tail latency during the failover window.

Attached is a short capacity workbook with suggested warm-up counts and estimated token cost for the failover window (capacity-plan.xlsx).

— Marcus
Attachment: capacity-plan.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance

Hi Elena — following resolution, quick post-incident summary and next steps. Timeline (UTC):
- 07:40 2028-10-04: anomalous peering flaps detected by provider
- 07:55: Redwood automated routing shifted 12% of EU traffic to reserves
- 08:12: Priya notified customers and recommended header/DNS changes
- 08:35: HealthLytics applied X-Redwood-Region: us + DNS override (confirmed at 08:42)
- 10:04: Provider announced peering restoration; eu metrics normalized by 10:25

Preliminary root cause: transient BGP/peering instability at a single provider edge POP affecting eu-west-2. Impact was amplified because several edge POPs were concurrently rehoming traffic to a small set of fallback POPs causing capacity pressure.

Corrective actions we are taking:
- Short term: add two additional fallback POPs for eu-west-2 and increase autoscale burst limit for customers routed through those POPs.
- Mid term (30 days): implement active health-probing with faster failover (target <60s) and publish a revised failover checklist for customers.
- Compliance: we will send HealthLytics an attestation describing the temporary cross-region routing within 24 hours.

Please review the attached postmortem (postmortem-summary-20281005.docx) and the shared action doc. Let us know if you want a joint call with our infra ops team this week to review changes and any compliance artifacts.

Action requested from HealthLytics: confirm if you want Redwood to schedule the DNS swap/rollback maintenance window next Tuesday (2028-10-09) at 02:00 UTC for controlled rollback.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Attachment: postmortem-summary-20281005.docx

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthLytics: regional outage notice + immediate request reroute guidance

Thanks team — appreciated the rapid response and clear runbook. We accept the attestation and would like the scheduled rollback on 2028-10-09 02:00 UTC. Please include our compliance lead (compliance@healthlytics.com) on the attestation email.

— Elena
